mmff94_term_audit_summary.note: 'routing_bug_candidate' = this exact atom-type tuple HAS a table row, just at a different classification/angle-type code than the one this molecule's context computed -- a candidate for a classification-derivation bug (angle_type_for/torsion_type_for/bond_type_for), not necessarily a genuine table gap. 'table_gap' = absent at EVERY classification code -- a genuine chematic-ff table gap under chematic's OWN existing fallback tiers. For Bond/Angle/Torsion/Oop, 'table_gap' is NOT further sub-classified this round (chematic-ff implements neither MMFF94 equivalence-class substitution nor empirical-rule estimation for these term kinds at all -- Mmff94NumericTypeInfo.equivalence_levels is parsed but has zero readers anywhere in the codebase, verified) -- deferred, not fabricated. For StretchBend specifically, 'table_gap' IS further sub-classified via 'stretch_bend_table_gap_breakdown' below: a diagnostic-only (never wired into production) port of RDKit's REAL stretch-bend fallback path, verified against the pinned RDKit commit (scripts/mmff94_provenance/PROVENANCE.md) -- confirmed RDKit's stretch-bend resolution is exactly (1) specific/generic MMFF-type lookup (matches chematic's existing mmff94_stbn chain) then (2) MMFFDfsbCollection's periodic-table-row default fallback (29-row table, ported here) -- NO equivalence-class step exists in RDKit's real stretch-bend path at all (eqLevel is used only by RDKit's angle/torsion/OOP fallback functions), so a stretch-bend 'equivalence_fallback_resolvable' bucket does not apply under RDKit's own algorithm, not just unmeasured here.

stretch_bend_table_gap_breakdown.note: dfsb_default_resolvable = would RDKit's MMFFDfsbCollection::getMMFFDfsbParams periodic-table-row default resolve this triple. This is RDKit's actual, complete residual fallback for stretch-bend (verified: no further mechanism exists after Dfsb in RDKit's real code path) -- so 'truly_unsupported_under_rdkits_own_algorithm' is a real claim (RDKit itself would also lack this parameter), not a hedge.
